To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bisection points of the intensity intervals were dependent upon the distribution of stimuli presented in generalizations.
the bisection location of the 90- to 50-decibels sound-intensity interval is a function of the distribution of stimuli presented in generalizaton.

(1) the bisection value varied systematically with the distribution of general stimuli presented in the context of the bisection test, (2) the bisections of the two animals were not significantly different, (3) the biseections of the two animals did not differ significantly from each other, and (4) the biselections of the two animals differed significantly from each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of varying the generalization stimuli upon the bisections of an auditory intensity interval.
the effects of the distribution of stimuli on the bisection points of intensity intervals.
the effect of stimulus distribution on the bisection judgment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bisection points were not constant across generalization distributions, and the effect of generalization distribution was to shift the bisection toward the training stimulus that was presented more often in generalization.
the bisection procedure, as used here, is sensitive to variations in the generalization gradient.

the effects of the distribution of generalizations stimuli within a constant intensity range upon the bissction of the intensity range by rats is a function of the relative frequency of response A. (Author/DB)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bisection is not an invariant property of the organism.
the distribution of generalizations stimuli within a constant generalization range affects the bisection points for the stimuli.
the bisection is determined by the context in which the stimuli are presented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bisection is not a fixed property of an organism but a property of an organism in context.
the bisection procedure can be used to study the effects of stimulus distribution on psychophysical judgments.
context effects are not unique to humans and that the effects of context are not necessarily due to a failure to attend to or remember the context in which the stimuli were presented.
